title: Vredefort impact
summary: An asteroid at least 10 km across struck what is now South Africa about 2.02 billion years ago. The IUGS describes the eroded Vredefort Dome, about 90 km across, as the remnant of an impact structure that was originally over 250 km in diameter, the largest known on Earth. The site was inscribed as a World Heritage property in 2005.

uncertainty.note: The opened pages give no uncertainty for the age, so none is claimed here. Years are Ma counted back from the present with no 1950 offset.

where.modern_name: Vredefort Dome, north-central South Africa, roughly 120 km southwest of Johannesburg
where.historical_name: Site of the future Vredefort Dome in what is now north-central South Africa; no polities exist at this date

paleo.not_applicable: The MERDITH2021 plate model used by the project only reaches 1000 Ma; this event is about 2023 Ma.

importance.justification: The largest known impact structure on Earth, a World Heritage property that exposes a full geological profile below the crater floor.

reviewer_note: Least sure of the age: IUCN gives 2,023 million years, IUGS 2.02 Ga and NASA only "about two billion years"; the opened pages state no error bar. IUGS calls it the second-oldest known impact structure, while the IUCN page calls it the oldest. Pin is the IUGS dome coordinates; uncertainty is half the stated original diameter.
